overview:
Israel is a narrow country on the eastern shore of the Mediterranean Sea, bordered by Lebanon, Syria, Jordan and Egypt. It is about 20,800 km², a little smaller than the US state of New Jersey, yet it contains snowy mountains, fertile valleys, the Negev desert and the lowest place on Earth's land surface, the Dead Sea. About 9.5 million people live there.

Hebrew is the main language, revived from ancient texts to become a living tongue spoken by millions, and Arabic is spoken by Israel's Arab citizens, about a fifth of the population. Most Israelis are Jewish, with roots in Europe, the Middle East, North Africa and Ethiopia. Israel considers Jerusalem its capital, though its status is disputed and most countries keep their embassies in Tel Aviv, the lively business and technology center on the coast.

Israel is a parliamentary democracy with an elected Knesset and prime minister. It is known for high-tech inventions, farms that bloom in the desert, and holy sites sacred to Jews, Christians and Muslims. The neighboring West Bank and Gaza Strip are Palestinian territories whose future remains unresolved.
landAndNature:
Israel packs many landscapes into a small space. The Mediterranean coastal plain is warm and fertile. Inland, hills rise to Jerusalem and the Galilee, and Mount Hermon in the far north gets enough snow for skiing. The Jordan River flows south into the Sea of Galilee, the lowest freshwater lake in the world, and on into the Dead Sea, about 430 meters below sea level, so salty that swimmers float like corks and no fish can live in it.

The Negev desert covers more than half the country, with the giant Ramon Crater, a huge eroded valley. At the southern tip, Eilat's coral reefs on the Red Sea shimmer with tropical fish. Israel lies on a major bird migration route, and half a billion birds pass over each spring and autumn. The hoopoe, with its striped crest, is the national bird.
peopleAndCulture:
Israeli society is a blend of Jewish communities from dozens of countries plus Arab Muslims, Christians, Druze and Bedouin. The week pauses for Shabbat from Friday evening to Saturday night, when buses stop in many cities and families gather for dinner. On Yom Kippur, the holiest day, roads fall silent and children ride bikes down empty highways. Passover, Hanukkah and Purim, with its costumes, are widely celebrated, as are Ramadan and Christmas in Arab communities.

Food is Middle Eastern at heart: hummus, falafel in pita, shakshuka eggs in tomato sauce, and fresh salads at breakfast. Soccer and basketball are the favorite sports. Israel calls itself the Start-Up Nation for its many tech companies, and inventions developed here include drip irrigation and the cherry tomato variety sold around the world.
history:
Ancient Israelite kingdoms ruled these hills about 3,000 years ago, and Jerusalem's Temple became the center of Jewish worship. Rome destroyed the Second Temple in 70 AD and scattered the Jewish people, while the land passed through Byzantine, Arab, Crusader, Mamluk and Ottoman hands and its population became largely Arab. In the late 1800s Jews began returning under the Zionist movement, and Britain governed the area after World War I.

After the Holocaust killed six million Jews in Europe, the United Nations proposed dividing the land into Jewish and Arab states. Israel declared independence on May 14, 1948, and war with neighboring Arab countries followed; hundreds of thousands of Palestinians became refugees. Israel captured the West Bank, Gaza and other lands in 1967, made peace with Egypt in 1979 and Jordan in 1994, and signed accords with the Palestinians in 1993, but conflict has continued, including a devastating war in Gaza from 2023.
funFacts: The Dead Sea shore is the lowest dry land on Earth, about 430 meters below sea level, and its water is nearly ten times saltier than the ocean.
Hebrew is the only ancient language ever revived to become the everyday speech of millions of native speakers.
About 500 million birds fly over Israel twice a year, making it one of the busiest migration corridors on the planet.
Drip irrigation, which waters plants drop by drop through thin tubes, was developed in Israel in the 1960s.
Masada, a mountaintop fortress by the Dead Sea, was the last stronghold of Jewish rebels against Rome in 73 AD.
Israel's national bird, the hoopoe, was chosen by a public vote in 2008 to mark the country's 60th birthday.
